key_insight: CompressionBench studies whether coding agents can autonomously compress pretrained LLMs while preserving their behavior under a smaller storage budget. The provided abstract describes the task setup but does not report performance results.
problem_solved: Can AI coding agents turn a source LLM checkpoint into a smaller model while respecting storage, inference-environment, and time constraints?
method: Frame LLM compression as a terminal-based task for a coding agent.
Provide a source checkpoint, storage limit, inference environment, and time budget.
Have the agent construct compressed weights, targeting behavior preservation within the allowed storage.
impact: This work offers a concrete setting for studying AI systems that improve the efficiency of models used by subsequent systems. For practitioners, it targets automated compression workflows, though the supplied excerpt does not establish their effectiveness.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: source checkpoint → coding agent → compressed model.
Constraint icons: storage budget, time limit, and inference environment.
Conceptual trade-off chart: model storage versus behavior preservation, without invented results.
Feedback-loop diagram connecting model compression to recursive self-improvement.
paper_title: CompressionBench: How can your coding agents compress LLMs?
paper_authors: Xinrui Zhong, Zhifeng Li, Zhiming Wang, Yongqi Liu, Shanglin Yang
